turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - b3_fatigue_train.csv: 293 real samples, columns process/composition
    columns (NT, THT, THt, THQCr, CT, Ct, DT, Dt, QmT, TT, Tt, TCr, C, Si,
    Mn, P, S, Ni, Cr, Cu, Mo, RedRatio, dA, dB, dC) and `target` (the
    measured rotating-bending fatigue strength (MPa)).
  - b3_fatigue_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE samples whose rotating-bending
    fatigue strength (MPa) was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and the
    same process/composition columns.

Using the training data, predict which candidates have the HIGHEST rotating-
bending fatigue strength (MPa), then select the 5 best candidates from the
pool.

Reason from the training data, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
The training data show a clear process-based separation in rotating-bending fatigue strength. Ordinary quenched-and-tempered heats (NT/THT in the 825–900 °C range, TT = 550–680 °C) never exceed ~650 MPa. High-Si spring-steel heats reach at most ~900 MPa. All values above 1000 MPa (and the global maximum of 1144 MPa) belong to the carburizing family (CT = 930 °C, DT \(\approx\) 850–900 °C, TT = 160 or 200 °C).

Within that family the dominant empirical trends are:
- lower QmT (60 °C vs 140 °C) and lower TT (160 °C vs 200 °C) raise strength by 20–60 MPa,
- higher case-depth parameters (Ct, Dt) are beneficial for the Ni-Cr-Mo chemistries that already produce the highest numbers,
- low P/S, high Cr or high Ni+RedRatio, and low inclusion ratings (dA/dB/dC) are advantageous.

Applying these trends by nearest-neighbour matching to the 11 carburized candidates in the pool yields the following point estimates (MPa):

- c081 (identical chemistry and process to the 1144 MPa record except TT = 200 °C) \(\approx\) 1110
- c053 (identical chemistry to the 1110 MPa heat, better TT, modestly lower Ct) \(\approx\) 1095
- c063 (high-Ct, QmT = 60 °C, TT = 160 °C, chemistry of the 1034/1082 pair) \(\approx\) 1080
- c016 (high-Ct, QmT = 60 °C, chemistry of the 1082 MPa heat, TT = 200 °C) \(\approx\) 1050
- c018 (same process window as c016, chemistry of the 1034 MPa heat) \(\approx\) 1050

All remaining candidates lie at or below 1040 MPa. Consequently the five highest-ranked members of the pool are c081, c053, c063, c016 and c018.

Final: c081, c053, c063, c016, c018
